boilerplate.general_comments_title: General Comments about the Quantitative Reasoning Section
general_comments: The figures accompanying some of the problems are provided to help solve the problems, but are not necessarily drawn to scale.  Therefore, do not rely on the figures alone to deduce line length, angle size, and so forth.
If a line in a figure appears to be straight, you may assume that it is in fact a straight line.
When a geometric term (side, radius, area, volume, etc.) appears in a problem, it refers to a term whose value is greater than 0, unless stated otherwise.
When \(\sqrt{a}\) (a > 0) appears in a problem, it refers to the positive root of a.
"0" is neither a positive nor a negative number.

clusters.intro: Study the graph below, then answer the four questions that follow. In a certain office a project was carried out in which 9 employees took part: 3 architects, 3 planners and 3 graphic artists. In the course of the work on the project the employees met with one another, and two employees took part in every meeting. The employees are marked in the graph by the letters A–I. Each cell in the graph describes the joint work of a pair of employees: the bold number indicates the total of all the meetings that took place between them, and the number in parentheses indicates the number of meetings between them that were defined as “effective”. A bold frame around a cell indicates that the pair of employees wrote a joint report (see key). Note: no pair wrote more than one joint report. For example, the bottom-left cell describes the joint work of employee A (who is an architect) and employee I (who is a graphic artist). Between employee A and employee I 3 meetings took place, and three of them were effective. The two employees did not write a joint report in the framework of the project.

Study the graphs below, then answer the four questions that follow. The graphs describe the effects of an experimental preparation for encouraging hair growth on a group of patients over the course of nine months. The data of each month represent the state of the group of patients at the end of that month (relative to the day on which the trial began). The upper part of the graphs describes the proportion of patients who experienced an improvement in the state of hair loss, the proportion of patients who experienced a worsening in the state of hair loss, and the proportion of patients who experienced the side effect of scales. A patient may be included in both of the groups of patients who experienced an improvement or a worsening and also in the group of those suffering from scales (but cannot be included in both the “improvement” group and the “worsening” group). The lower part of the graphs presents, of all those patients, the proportion of those on whom the effect was of a degree defined as “great”. The rest of the patients experienced that same effect to a degree defined as “slight”. Remarks: – The lines connecting the data of the months are aid lines only. – The number of patients in the trial remained fixed throughout. For example, after one month of using the preparation 5% of the patients experienced some degree of improvement. 35% of those 5% experienced an improvement to a great degree, and hence 65% of them experienced an improvement to a slight degree.

questions.stem: Given: \(x - y < y - x\) Which of the following inequalities is necessarily true?

methods.text: Add \(x\) to both sides and add \(y\) to neither: \(x-y<y-x\) gives \(2x<2y\), so \(x<y\).
The two sides are the same gap measured in opposite directions. Saying one is smaller than the other is just saying which of \(x\) and \(y\) is further right.
\(x=1,\ y=2\) satisfies the given and makes both \(x\) and \(x+y\) positive, so (1) and (2) are not forced; \(x=-2,\ y=-1\) satisfies it with both negative, confirming it.

questions.stem:
5 people met, and each of them shook hands once (and only once) with every one of the others.

How many handshakes were exchanged?
The figure before you is a pentagon. According to the data in the figure, what is necessarily the size of \(\beta\)?

On every day of the month whose date is even, Dani buys products for a total of 18 shekels.
On every day of the month whose date is odd, Dani buys products for a total of 12 shekels.

A certain month has 30 days.  For how many shekels in total does Dani buy products in that month?

methods.text: A 30-day month has 15 even and 15 odd dates: \(15 \times 18 + 15 \times 12 = 450\).
Equal counts only because the month has an even number of days. A 31-day month would give 16 odd dates and a different answer.

questions.stem:
Squares were built on the sides of an isosceles trapezoid.  The sum of the areas of the squares built on the bases equals the sum of the areas of the squares built on the legs.

According to these data and the data in the figure,

\(\dfrac{a}{b} = ?\)

\(A\), \(B\), \(C\) and \(D\) are the letters representing different digits, all between 1 and 9. Given: \(\begin{array}{r}AB\\+\ AB\\\hline CDA\end{array}\) Which of the following claims is necessarily true?

methods.text: \(\overline{AB} + \overline{AB} = 2\overline{AB}\), which is even — so its units digit \(A\) must be even. That settles it in one line.

The result \(\overline{CDA}\) is three digits, so \(2\overline{AB} \ge 100\) and \(\overline{AB} \ge 50\), which pins \(A\) to 6 or 8. Either way \(A\) is even, and nothing is forced about \(B\), \(C\) or \(D\).

questions.stem:
\(x\) is a positive number.

Given:  \(120!\cdot 121! = (120!)^2\cdot x^2\)

\(x = ?\)

methods.text: \(121!=121\cdot120!\), so the left side is \(121\cdot(120!)^2\). Setting that equal to \((120!)^2x^2\) cancels the squares outright, leaving \(x^2=121\) and \(x=11\).
The enormous numbers are decoration. The only thing that matters is that \(121!\) and \(120!\) are neighbours, so their ratio is the single factor 121 — and 121 is a perfect square.

questions.stem:
Given:  \(|a| \ne |b|\)

\(\dfrac{a}{a-b} - \dfrac{b}{a+b} = ?\)

methods.text: Over the common denominator \((a-b)(a+b) = a^2-b^2\), the numerator is \(a(a+b) - b(a-b) = a^2+ab-ab+b^2 = a^2+b^2\). So the value is \(\dfrac{a^2+b^2}{a^2-b^2}\).
Take \(a=3, b=1\): the expression is \(\frac32 - \frac14 = \frac54\), and \(\frac{9+1}{9-1} = \frac{10}{8} = \frac54\).
The condition \(|a| \neq |b|\) is there to keep \(a^2-b^2\) non-zero — the denominator the factorisation is about to produce.

questions.stem: Out of all the meetings that employee D held, the largest number of meetings was with employee –
Of the pairs of employees in which exactly one employee is an architect, how many pairs wrote a joint report?

A “successful pair” is a pair of employees who had at least four effective meetings.

Of the pairs in which at least one employee is a graphic artist, how many pairs are successful pairs?
One of the pairs of employees wrote a joint report after having exactly 3 meetings that were not effective. What is necessarily true regarding the two employees in this pair?
options: They do not have the same profession
At least one of them is a graphic artist
At least one of them is a planner

options: It cannot be determined from the data

questions.stem: \(M\) is a whole number. Given: the value of the expression \((M-1)(M-2)\) is divisible by 3. Which of the three following numbers is certainly not divisible by 3?
options: It cannot be determined which of the above numbers is not divisible by 3

methods.text: Among any three consecutive integers, exactly one is divisible by 3. Here \(M-2\), \(M-1\) and \(M\) are three in a row, and the given says one of the first two carries the factor of 3.
So \(M\) itself cannot be the one — the multiple of 3 has already been used up. \(M+1\) and \(M+2\) are not pinned either way, which is why only \(M\) is certain.

questions.stem: In a class there are 40 pupils. 50% of the pupils have black hair. 40% of the pupils have ginger hair. 25% of the pupils have blue eyes. It is known that 10% of the pupils whose hair colour is black have blue eyes. Of the pupils whose hair is ginger, how many at least have blue eyes?

methods.text:
Of 40 pupils: 20 black-haired, 16 ginger, 10 blue-eyed, and 2 of the black-haired have blue eyes. That leaves 8 blue-eyed pupils among the other 20, of whom 16 are ginger and 4 are neither.

At worst all 4 non-ginger take a blue-eyed slot, leaving \(8 - 4 = 4\) for the gingers.
“At least” means assume the worst distribution, exactly as with the air-conditioned cars. These minimum-overlap questions are a recurring shape.

questions.stem:
A vehicle covers one kilometre in 72 seconds.

What is the speed of the vehicle in kph?

methods.text: \(\frac{3600}{72} = 50\) kilometres an hour, since there are 3600 seconds in an hour and each kilometre costs 72 of them.
Scaling up instead: 72 seconds is \(1.2\) minutes, and \(\frac{60}{1.2} = 50\). Either route, the move is to ask how many of these trips fit in an hour.

In the figure before you, point \(O\) is the centre of the circle.
\(A\), \(B\) and \(C\) are points on the circumference of the circle.
\(ABOC\) is a parallelogram.

How many different sizes can the angle \(\sphericalangle BOC\) have?

Given:  \(x^{2n} = x^{-n}\) ,  \(x \ne 0\) ,  \(n \ne 0\)

Which of the following claims is correct?

methods.text: Same base, so \(2n = -n\) would need \(3n = 0\), impossible. The equality therefore comes from the base: \(x^{3n} = 1\), which for odd \(n\) forces \(x = 1\), and for even \(n\) allows \(x = \pm1\).
\(x=-1, n=2\) satisfies the given and breaks options (1) and (2) at once, leaving the odd-\(n\) pair. Then \(x=-1\) with odd \(n\) fails the equation, which rules out option (4).

questions.stem:
In the figure before you is a cylinder inside which are two cones.
\(AB\) is a diameter of the bottom base of the cylinder, and \(O\) is the centre of this base.
The radius of the base of the cylinder is \(r\), and the height of the cylinder is \(h\).
\(AO\) and \(BO\) are radii of the bases of the two cones, and the height of the cones is \(h\).

\(\dfrac{\text{the sum of the volumes of the cones}}{\text{the volume of the cylinder}} = ?\)

At a certain bank there is a commission of 0.25 shekels for every shekel that is converted into foreign currency.
Leah has 1,000 shekels.  She wants to buy bolivianos at this bank, the currency of the state of Bolivia, whose exchange rate for one unit is 0.5 shekels.

How many bolivianos will Leah be able to buy with the sum she has, if this sum must also serve her to pay the commission?

methods.text: The commission is 0.25 per shekel converted, so each shekel of foreign currency costs 1.25 shekels. Her 1,000 shekels therefore convert 800 shekels' worth.

At 0.5 shekels per boliviano, 800 shekels buys \(\frac{800}{0.5} = 1{,}600\) bolivianos.

Option (3) comes from taking 25% off the result rather than off the amount converted.

questions.stem: An adult cat eats 1 kg of food in two weeks. A kitten eats half the amount of food that an adult cat eats. How many kg of food does a kitten eat in a week?

methods.text: An adult eats \(\frac12\) kg a week, so a kitten eats \(\frac14\).
Two conversions in one step — halve for the week, halve again for the kitten. Doing only one gives \(\frac12\), which is option (2).

questions.stem:
In the figure before you, \(ABC\) is a right-angled isosceles triangle.
\(ADEF\) is a square.
The length of the segment \(DB\) equals the perimeter of the square \(ADEF\).

\(\dfrac{\text{the area of the square }ADEF}{\text{the area of the triangle }ABC} = ?\)

methods.text: Expand the left: \(x^2 + 6x + 9 = x^2 - 3\). The \(x^2\) cancels, leaving \(6x = -12\) and \(x = -2\).
It looks quadratic and is not — the squared terms cancel. Recognising that before reaching for the quadratic formula is the whole point.

questions.stem:
In the figure before you, \(a\) and \(b\) are two straight lines that intersect each other.

Given:  \(\gamma = \beta\)

\(\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta} + \dfrac{\gamma}{\alpha} = ?\)

methods.text: \(xy = \dfrac{(x+y)^2 - (x-y)^2}{4} = \dfrac{4-4}{4} = 0\). The pivot from the algebraic expressions lesson, with both ingredients supplied.
The two numbers are \(0\) and \(-2\): they sum to \(-2\) and differ by 2 in size. Their product is 0.

questions.stem:
In the system of axes before you is an octagon whose vertices' coordinates are whole numbers.

What is the area of the octagon?

A pool is filled with water up to \(\dfrac{3}{5}\) of its volume.
After 21 cubic metres of water were drawn from it, the remaining water filled only \(\dfrac{1}{4}\) of the volume of the pool.

What is the volume of the pool (in cubic metres)?

methods.text: The 21 m³ corresponds to the difference between the two fractions, not to either one. Subtracting the fractions first is the whole question.

questions.stem:
The operation \(\$\) is defined for every two whole numbers \(x\) and \(y\) thus:  \(\$(x,y) = 2(x-y)\)
\(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) are three consecutive whole numbers, \(a < b < c\).

\(\$(\,\$(a,b)\,,\,\$(b,c)\,) = ?\)

methods.text: Square the given: \(x = 4y\). Then \(x^2 = 16y^2\).
\(y=1\): \(\sqrt x = 2\), so \(x = 4\) and \(x^2 = 16 = 16y^2\). The other options give 1, 2 and 8.

questions.stem:
Given:  \(x\) is divisible by 10 and by 15.

By which of the following numbers is \(x\) necessarily divisible?

methods.text: Divisible by 10 and by 15 means divisible by their LCM. \(10 = 2 \cdot 5\) and \(15 = 3 \cdot 5\), so the LCM is \(2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5 = 30\) — not 150.
\(6\) divides 30 ✓. \(20\) needs two factors of 2, \(25\) needs two 5s, and \(50\) needs both — none is guaranteed. Take \(x = 30\) and all three fail at once.

questions.stem:
Alon, Baruch, Gilya and Dana prepared paper aeroplanes.
The number of aeroplanes Baruch made equals the number of aeroplanes Gilya and Dana made together.
If we subtract from the number of aeroplanes Alon made the number of aeroplanes Gilya made, Alon will still have more aeroplanes than Dana.

Which of the following claims is necessarily correct?
options: Alon has more aeroplanes than Baruch
Baruch has more aeroplanes than Alon
Gilya has more aeroplanes than Dana
Dana has more aeroplanes than Gilya

methods.text: Translate each sentence into an equation and compare the totals; the question asks only which of two people has more, so a full solution is not needed.
Comparisons are often decidable from the relationships alone, without finding any individual count.

questions.stem:
A box of matches in the shape of a box is placed on a table.
Elisheva rolls the box on the table in several stages: at each stage she turns the box so that its position remains in place.
The figure describes the five positions the box passed through, from a side view.
\(A\) is the point that was at the bottom-left corner of the box in the initial position.

In the same side view, where was point \(A\) located in the final position?

Every morning the height of the snow that fell at a certain ski resort is measured.
On the morning of the first day of a certain week the height of the snow was 100 cm.  Every day that week the height of the snow decreased by \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) of its height in the previous measurement.

On the morning of which day was a height of snow smaller than 5 cm measured for the first time?
options: That week no height of snow smaller than 5 cm was measured

methods.text: Each day multiplies the height by \(\frac23\): 100, 66.7, 44.4, 29.6, 19.8, 13.2, 8.8.
Read off the first day the height falls below the stated threshold. Repeated multiplication, not repeated subtraction — the fraction is of the current height.

In a sack there are 9 balls: 8 silver balls and one gold ball.  Yaron draws 2 balls from the sack at random, one after the other, and places them on the table.

What is the chance that one of the two balls on the table will be the gold ball?

A regular hexagon circumscribes a circle whose radius is \(r\) (see figure).

What is the length of the side of the hexagon?

The sum of \(n\) numbers (\(3 \le n\)) is larger by \(x\) than their average.

What is the sum of the numbers?

Given: at the end of month 2 of the trial, 1,200 of the patients experienced the side effect of scales.

How many patients took part in the trial altogether?
In how many months was the number of patients who experienced a great improvement equal to the number of patients who experienced a slight improvement?
Out of all the participants, what is the proportion of patients who experienced a great improvement in hair loss at the end of month 3?
Which of the following situations is possible?
options: There is a participant who experienced a great worsening in hair loss at the end of each one of the months of the trial
There is a participant who suffered from scales to a slight degree at the end of month 5 of the trial
